title: Sub-Scope Returned Package Review Delivery
summary: allow a returned sub-scope package to reach immutable Docs Review without implying canonical Import
content_html:
Sub-Scope Returned Package Review Delivery

Result

Delivered as SRR-1 after Sub-Scope Package Preparation Delivery.

One complete returned package prepared from an exact { scope, sub_scope } collection can be validated and materialized as an immutable, read-only Docs Review package. It does not mutate canonical sub-scope documents.

The delivery stopped after real Docs Review acceptance. A realistic 249-document Analysis/Tags package was inspected successfully, and the accepted next decision is a separate Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery.

Capability Split

Reviewability and importability are separate trusted capabilities:

package capability supports_docs_review supports_return_import
normal document-content true true
sub-scope document-content true false
fully export-only package false false

false / true is invalid: an importable returned package must also be reviewable.

SSI-3 remains honestly export-only for canonical mutation. SRR-1 allows its trusted returned package to enter Docs Review without making it actionable in Docs Viewer Import. Existing top-level package behavior remains unchanged, but its profile projection, export metadata, returned-package listing, Docs Review manifest, and endpoint validation are retrofitted to carry and enforce both flags explicitly.

Review Package checks supports_docs_review; Docs Viewer Import independently checks supports_return_import. Neither capability is inferred from the other. Existing stored packages that carry only supports_return_import from the prior single-flag contract are deprecated and must be regenerated. SRR-1 adds no compatibility fallback or metadata migration.

Review-Only Contract

  • Trusted metadata retains scope, sub_scope, export/profile identity, and the exact prepared selected_doc_ids.
  • Returned rows must equal that complete prepared set. Missing, extra, duplicate, malformed, or cross-collection IDs block the package.
  • The configured child collection is flat. Returned parent hierarchy is not applied or used to invent sub-scope structure.
  • The existing scope-owned Review Package Action lists the staged package with its parent scope and sub-scope label. This is not another sub-scope selection action.
  • Review materialization remains idempotent and publishes one docs_review_validated_package_v1 folder containing the complete returned record set and provenance.
  • Docs Review remains isolated and read-only. It has no canonical Save, Import, or query-string handoff.
  • Docs Viewer Import and direct import endpoints continue to reject the package while supports_return_import is false.

Import Decision

SRR-1 proved faithful review and did not add canonical mutation. The accepted follow-on is SRR-2, a separate delivery that must retain exact { scope, sub_scope } provenance, flat document semantics, whole-package validation, one package-level confirmation, stale-source protection, and all-or-nothing apply.

Delivery Tracker

[x] SRR-1.0 — Split Review And Import Capability

  • [x] Add explicit trusted Docs Review eligibility without weakening the existing Import blocker.
  • [x] Keep top-level packages and historical trusted-package validation behavior explicit.

[x] SRR-1.1 — Materialize Sub-Scope Docs Review

  • [x] Extend returned listing, validation, provenance, and review projection with exact sub_scope.
  • [x] Prove atomic identity validation, flat projection, idempotent reopen, and direct Import rejection with synthetic packages.

SRR-1.0–1.1 Evidence

  • Profiles, package results, trusted export metadata, external context, returned rows, and Docs Review manifests now carry both capabilities. Top-level document-content remains true / true; sub-scope document-content is true / false; the tree profile is false / false. Missing, non-boolean, and false / true metadata fail closed.
  • Review listing and direct review validate supports_docs_review; the CLI parser and direct Import independently validate supports_return_import. Review rows show parent-scope and configured sub-scope labels.
  • A synthetic two-document library/tags return retained its exact prepared IDs and provenance, materialized both documents as roots, reopened the same immutable review package idempotently, exposed no canonical sub-scope query-string link, and remained absent from Docs Import. Cross-collection selected IDs were rejected.
  • Focused Python coverage passed 112 passed, 1 skipped. The Review Package module, real manage-route, and Docs Review service smokes passed, as did explicit Python and JavaScript lint and git diff --check.
  • The realistic 20260730-095512-documents-document-content.jsonl package listed Analysis / Tags with 249 documents and opened successfully in Docs Review. No canonical document source was changed, and no SRR-2 Import path was added.

[x] SRR-1.2 — Review And Stop

  • [x] Inspect a realistic returned tag-document package in Docs Review.
  • [x] Record whether canonical source updates remain manual or justify a separate SRR-2 Import delivery.

Completion Gate

Met. One trusted returned sub-scope package opens as a complete read-only Docs Review package, cannot reach canonical Import, and leaves a deliberate, separately documented Import delivery rather than an implied mutation path.
